s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of vertigo and imbalance with gradual progression to constant dizziness
key_facts: 75-year-old woman
Presumed stroke in April 2020
Slurred speech, imbalance, and confusion lasting 48 hours in 2020
Brain MRI showed chronic periventricular white matter changes without acute ischemic lesions in 2020
CT angiography demonstrated carotid tortuosity with stenosis from myointimal plaques in 2020
Medications included barnidipine, clopidogrel, and atorvastatin
Recurrent dizzying attacks since 2020
Normal general and neurologic examinations at the first visit
Low mood reported at the first visit
Severe dizziness worsened by movement or position change
Normal vital signs
Normal speech
Intact strength and sensation
Normal reflexes and cranial nerves
Weakly positive finger-nose test on the right
Negative HINTS examination

shortlist.label: Vestibular Migraine
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of vertigo and imbalance with gradual progression to constant dizziness, normal examinations, and lack of clear central or peripheral vestibular origin

shortlist.label: Meniere's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic vertigo, imbalance, and progression to constant dizziness, despite negative HINTS examination

shortlist.label: Multiple System Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive imbalance, gait disturbance, and autonomic dysfunction, with normal strength and sensation

shortlist.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual progression of ataxia, imbalance, and gait disturbance, with normal examinations and lack of clear central or peripheral vestibular origin

shortlist.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of ataxia, imbalance, and vertigo, with normal examinations and lack of clear central or peripheral vestibular origin

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent dizzying attacks, unsteadiness, and wide-based gait, along with the progression to constant dizziness and loss of autonomy, are consistent with Multiple System Atrophy. The normal general and neurologic examinations, combined with the lack of evidence for central or peripheral vestibular origin, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Vestibular Migraine
rejected.why: The absence of nausea or vomiting and the lack of headache during episodes make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Meniere's Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic vertigo, tinnitus, and hearing loss of Meniere's Disease

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia
rejected.why: The patient's age of onset and the progression of symptoms are not typical for Spinocerebellar Ataxia

rejected.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 1
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are not consistent with the characteristic episodic ataxia and myokymia of Episodic Ataxia Type 1
